WCD_calculation.general_equation: WCD_f = S*C + L*tp + S*ts + S*te, where L = hop_count (links), S = L - 1 (switches), C=50us, tp=1us/link, ts=1us/switch, te=1us/switch
WCD_calculation.per_hop_interference: bounded to one CQF cycle per switch hop (no same-priority interference carry-over between cycles under CQF)

missing_inputs: Frame serialization time relative to 50us CQF cycle: at 100 Mbps, max bytes per 50us cycle is 625B; several given payloads exceed this and would require fragmentation or larger cycles, neither specified.
Exact TAS gate open/close times (guard bands) per port/cycle are not provided; assumed 0us guard band and that gates align to allow one-cycle forwarding per hop.
Whether end systems implement CQF gating was not specified; assumed CQF applies at switches only with source offset at t=0.
Header/CRC/preamble size (on-the-wire frame length) not provided; payload used only to report but not included in WCD due to CQF cycle abstraction.
Exact application of time synchronization error (per hop vs per path) is not specified; applied per switch hop here for worst case.

assumptions: Network-wide CQF gating is synchronized; frames generated at t=0 can transmit in cycle 0 at the source.
At each switch hop, CQF introduces exactly one full-cycle latency (frame transmitted in the next cycle).
Per-link propagation = 1 µs; per-switch cut-through forwarding latency = 1 µs.
End-to-end delay measured until the last bit of the frame is received at the destination.
Serialization time is computed from payload bytes only (no L2/L1 overhead specified).
Time synchronization error modeled as a fixed 2 µs margin end-to-end.

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = s*C + T_tx_last + h*T_prop + s*T_sw + T_sync_margin

variable_definitions.s: number of switches on the path = h - 1
variable_definitions.T_tx_last: serialization time on last hop = payload_B * 8 / (100e6) seconds = payload_B * 0.08 µs

notes: Under CQF, each switch hop forwards in the subsequent cycle; the source transmits in the initial cycle (offset set to 0), so cycle contribution equals s*C.
Serialization within intermediate hops is contained inside each cycle; only the last hop's serialization extends the end-to-end finish time.
This bound assumes guard bands/gate windows suffice to complete transmissions within their assigned cycles.

Whether end stations apply CQF gating on the first hop (source NIC); here, queuing cycle counted only per switch stage.
Any guard band configuration beyond 1 us sync error; no explicit guard band modeled.
Potential interference from non-TT traffic is assumed absent by problem statement; if present, would alter bounds.

all_parameters_used.cqf_behavior: Frames that arrive in cycle n are transmitted in cycle n+1 on each hop (two-buffer CQF).
notes: All flows are TT with PCP=7 and use the CQF two-queue pair: queue 7 on odd cycles, queue 6 on even cycles.
Cycle duration is 50 us. Hypercycle (LCM of all flow periods and cycle) is 375000 us.
Cut-through switching delay per bridge is modeled as 1 us.

WARNING: Several payloads have serialization time over 50 us at 100 Mbps. In strict two-buffer CQF, a frame's transmission typically must fit within the transmit cycle; this dataset would require multi-cycle transmission or larger cycle/bitrate. The WCD computed here still accounts for full serialization time on every link but assumes the CQF stage advance remains one cycle per hop.

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD_us = (H + 1) * C + H * (t_ser + t_prop) + (H - 1) * t_sw + t_sync

variables.H: hop_count (number of links on the path, from the provided routes)
variables.t_ser: serialization time per link = (8 * payload_bytes) / (100e6) seconds = 0.08 * payload_bytes us
variables.t_sw: cut-through switching delay per switch = 1 us

assumptions: Every hop advances the frame by exactly one CQF cycle (arrive in cycle n -> transmit in cycle n+1).
End stations inject at offset 0 and the first egress may wait up to one cycle.
CQF guard band and exact GCL phase not provided; entire cycle is available to the TT queue pair (6/7).
No additional blocking within a cycle is modeled beyond full per-link serialization accounted separately.
Ethernet L2 overhead (headers/preamble/IFG) is not provided; serialization uses payload bytes only.

missing_inputs: Exact L2 frame size (headers, VLAN tag(s), preamble/SFD, IFG) per flow

Confirmation whether end-stations implement CQF gating (or only bridges)
Clarification whether time synchronization error should be applied once end-to-end or per hop

Feasibility detail: With 100 Mbps and 50 us cycle, multiple payloads exceed a single-cycle transmit time; confirm whether multi-cycle transmission on the same egress queue is allowed or adjust cycle/bitrate

variables.Hs_i: number of switches along the route

notes: CQF adds at most one cycle of queuing per switching stage (peristaltic forwarding).
Cut-through is assumed; per-link serialization is accounted for by the CQF transmit window and not added separately.
All flows use TT with PCP=7 mapped to the CQF odd/even queue pair (7/6).

missing_inputs: Per-port gate control lists (GCLs), guard band durations, and exact CQF window sizing are not provided.
Frame overheads (L2 headers, preamble, IFG) are not specified; payload was treated as the schedulable frame size.

Some payloads exceed 625 Bytes; at 100 Mbps and 50 us cycle, their serialization would not fit a single window without preemption or larger T. We assumed windows are dimensioned accordingly (or that serialization is included in the CQF window), consistent with the CQF hop-per-cycle model.
Whether end stations implement CQF gating is not specified; analysis assumes CQF stages only at switches.
Exact latency measurement reference point (first bit in vs last bit out) is not specified; we use a standard CQF worst-case residence-time model at switch egress plus fixed delays.

assumptions: CQF is implemented at all switch egress ports; end-stations are time-aligned sources but do not add extra CQF stage
Frames arriving in cycle n are transmitted in cycle n+1 at each switch (one cycle per switch hop)
Time-sync error is accounted per switch hop as a safety margin
Serialization uses payload only (no L2 overhead specified), t_ser_per_link = payload_bytes * 8 / 100 Mbps = payload_bytes * 0.08 us

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = S*C + L*t_prop + S*t_sw + L*t_ser + S*e_sync, where S = hop_count - 1 (number of switches), L = hop_count (number of links)
notes: CQF adds exactly one cycle of store-and-forward delay per switch hop (frames that arrive in cycle n are transmitted in cycle n+1).
Propagation, switching, and serialization occur on each link; time-sync error is accounted as a per-switch margin.
Start offsets at sources are fixed to 0; no additional release jitter assumed.

missing_inputs: Exact per-port CQF transmit/receive phase alignment (odd/even mapping schedule) — assumed globally synchronized two-queue alternation

all_parameters_used.CQF_behavior_assumption: At each bridge egress, a frame arriving in cycle k is transmitted in cycle k+1 (worst-case wait <= 1 cycle). Time sync error is budgeted per bridge.
all_parameters_used.offset_setting: All flows start at t=0 at their source end-station.

WCD_calculation.general_equation: For each flow: H = hop_count (links), B = H-1 (number of bridge egresses). With cycle T=50 µs, per-bridge switching t_sw=1 µs, time sync error t_sync=1 µs, per-link propagation t_prop=1 µs, bandwidth=100 Mbps, payload L bytes: t_ser_per_link = 8*L/100e6 seconds = 0.08*L µs. Then WCD = B*(T + t_sw + t_sync) + H*(t_prop + t_ser_per_link).

missing_inputs: Exact L2 frame size per flow (preamble, SFD, MAC header, VLAN tag, FCS, IFG) — serialization computed from payload only.
Per-port CQF transmit/receive window alignment (phase) — assumed ideal alternating windows synchronized network-wide.
Exact guard band allocation policy vs sync error — we budgeted 1 µs per bridge.
Any per-ES shaping/gating — assumed none at ES (CQF only on bridges).
Physical link lengths (we used fixed 1 µs propagation per link).

assumptions: All TT flows with PCP=7 map to the CQF TT queue pair {7 on odd cycles, 6 on even cycles}.
Every switch egress that forwards a given flow alternates between queues 7 and 6 per cycle; thus each flow uses both queues over time at that egress.
Per-hop CQF latency contribution is one cycle per switching stage.
Serialization time is counted on every traversed link.
Propagation and switching delays are additive per link/switch.
Time synchronization error is added once end-to-end as a conservative bound.

WCD_calculation.equation: For a flow with hop_count h (number of links), payload B bytes, bandwidth R=100 Mbps, cycle C=50 µs, per-link propagation t_prop=1 µs, per-switch delay t_sw=1 µs, and time sync error T_sync=1 µs: t_ser = 8*B/R (µs) = 0.08*B (µs). Then WCD = (h-1)*C + h*(t_prop + t_ser) + (h-1)*t_sw + T_sync. Algebraically: WCD = h*t_ser + 52*h - 50 (µs).

missing_inputs: Per-frame Ethernet overhead (preamble, IFG, L2 headers) is not specified; serialization time was computed on payload bytes only.

CQF feasibility constraints (sum of frame times per cycle per egress, and t_ser <= C) are not provided; several payloads exceed the 50 µs cycle at 100 Mbps, which would be unschedulable in strict CQF unless larger cycle or fragmentation is used.
Exact gate control list phasing per port (cycle parity alignment) is not provided; we assumed standard CQF one-cycle-per-hop transfer independent of phase.
Definition of end-to-end delay reference (first bit to last bit vs. last bit to last bit) is not stated; we used last-bit arrival including serialization on every link.

WCD_calculation.equation: For each flow i: WCD_i = (H_i + 1)*T + H_i*t_prop + (H_i - 1)*t_sw + t_ser_last + 2*t_sync_err

term_definitions.t_sw: per-switch forwarding latency in cut-through (1 µs), applied to each intermediate switch (H-1 times)
term_definitions.t_ser_last: serialization time on the last hop = payload_bytes * 8 / (100e6) seconds = payload_B * 0.08 µs
term_definitions.t_sync_err: time synchronization error margin (1 µs); applied as 2*t_sync_err budget end-to-end

notes: CQF ensures per-hop residence time bounded to one cycle; the formula accounts for (H+1) cycles (source emission to last-hop transmit completion) plus fixed physical latencies and serialization on the final hop.
All flows are TT with PCP 7 and use only the CQF odd/even queues (7/6).
Egress queue used per switch alternates with cycle parity: even cycles -> Q6, odd cycles -> Q7.
